claims.text: The proposed multilayer coating consists of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi layers.
Previous work studied equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi bicrystals.
Decreasing layer thickness increases the density of multilayer interfaces.
Multilayer and homogeneous coatings can be compared at the same overall CoCrFeMnNi composition.
A high density of multilayer interfaces increases resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation.
Multilayer interfaces act similarly to twist grain boundaries.
The multilayer interfaces impede the nucleation of dislocations under sustained load.
The multilayer interfaces impede the propagation of dislocations under sustained load.
Twist grain boundaries affect dislocation nucleation in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Multilayer interfaces are barriers to dislocation motion and sites for dislocation trapping.
Multilayer interfaces generate local stress fields and mismatches.
Interface-generated stress fields and mismatches delay activation of dislocation sources.
Interrupting dislocation motion diminishes plastic-strain accumulation over time and therefore reduces creep deformation.
Higher-interface-density multilayer coatings will have a lower creep rate than homogeneous coatings of the same composition.
Higher-interface-density multilayer coatings will accumulate less plastic deformation over time than homogeneous coatings.
The reduced creep response will be accompanied by fewer and more localized dislocation activities.
The proposed mechanism applies when dislocation-based creep dominates and diffusion-driven creep and dynamic recrystallization are not activated.
The barrier effect requires the individual layer thickness to remain above a critical minimum.
The dependence of creep resistance on interface spacing is not yet quantitatively established.
A lack of statistically significant creep-rate, strain-accumulation, and dislocation-structure differences between multilayer and homogeneous coatings would falsify the hypothesis.
